svg.text: LINKEDIN — THE CONNECTION HANDSHAKE
THE HANDSHAKE — consent needs an ACTOR
① sendConnectionRequest(senderId, receiverId, message)
getUser(sender) · getUser(receiver) — both must exist, else UserNotFoundException
reject self-connect · reject a duplicate PENDING request · reject already-connected
→ new ConnectionRequest(requestId, sender, receiver), status = PENDING
② THE AUTHORIZATION GATE — requireRequestFor(reqId, responderId, action)
ConnectionRequest request = connectionRequests.get(requestId);
if (request == null) throw new RequestNotFoundException(...);
if (!request.getReceiverId().equals(responderId))
throw new IllegalStateException("Only the receiver can " + action + " ...");
Without the accepterId parameter the SENDER could accept their own request
and connect to anyone unilaterally. A consent handshake must know who consents.
③ ACCEPT — write BOTH sides of the edge
request.accept(); // status = ACCEPTED
sender.addConnection(receiver.getUserId());
receiver.addConnection(sender.getUserId()); // symmetric, same call
one logical edge, two set entries — written together so they cannot drift ✓
ConnectionRequest — RequestStatus
PENDING
accept() — receiver only
reject() — receiver only
ACCEPTED
REJECTED
ACCEPTED is what makes the pair 1st-degree, which is what the feed reads ✓
HONEST GAP: accept() / reject() do not guard the current status —
re-accepting an ACCEPTED request silently re-fires instead of throwing.
TWO EDGE KINDS, ONE STORAGE SHAPE
CONNECTION — mutual, consent-gated
Stored as TWO set entries for ONE logical edge:
alice.connectionIds = { bob }
bob.connectionIds = { alice }
Denormalized on purpose: getConnections(userId) is O(1) into the set,
then O(k) to hydrate — no scan of an edge table.
acceptConnection writes both entries in one method, so they can't diverge ✓
a real store makes this one edge row and derives both directions from it
FOLLOW — asymmetric, no consent
Also two set entries, but they mean different things:
follower.followingIds.add(followeeId); // "who I read"
followee.followerIds.add(followerId); // "who reads me"
No request, no accept, no reject — the edge exists the moment it is written.
THE BUG THIS SHAPE INVITES — and it was real here:
follow() wrote BOTH sides. unfollow() cleared only the follower's side.
The followee listed a stale follower permanently, and follower counts
drifted upward forever — a number that only ever grows.
THE RULE THAT PREVENTS IT
Any denormalized edge must have its write and its un-write written
as a pair, in the same review, touching the same fields.
unfollow() must mirror follow() exactly — both sides, or neither ✓
Same shape as Amazon's reserve/release and this repo's other saga compensations:
an operation without its inverse is only half-implemented.
NOT ATOMIC — say it before you're asked
Both writes are two separate statements on two plain HashSets. A crash or a
concurrent read between them sees a one-way edge. Single edge row, or a
transaction, is the real answer — the in-memory version is a single-node artifact.
WHAT AN ACCEPTED EDGE UNLOCKS
THE FEED — getFeed(userId, limit)
posts.values().stream()
.filter(p -> user.getConnectionIds().contains(p.getAuthorId())
|| user.getFollowingIds().contains(p.getAuthorId())
|| p.getVisibility() == PUBLIC) .sorted(newest).limit(limit)
1st-degree connections ∪ who you follow ∪ anything PUBLIC, chronological.
O(all posts) per call — there is no posts-by-author index, and no ranking
Strategy seam either: the ordering is hard-coded into the service.
ENDORSEMENTS — a set, never a counter
endorseSkill(userId, skillName, endorserId):
reject self-endorsement · resolve the named skill or throw
skill.endorse(endorserId)
private final Set<String> endorserIds = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
getEndorsements() returns endorserIds.size() — derived, never stored
re-endorsing is a no-op, not a +1. Withdrawing is exact. "Who endorsed me?"
is answerable. And it is the ONE concurrent collection in the model ✓
JOBS — a second content type with its own lifecycle
ACTIVE
closeJob(jobId)
CLOSED
searchJobs(query, location) filters ACTIVE first, then optional title-contains,
then optional location-contains. Both filters are null-tolerant by design.
O(all jobs) scan · no JobApplication entity — applying is out of scope here
THE FOLLOW-UP: DEGREES OF SEPARATION
Only 1st degree exists here. 2nd degree = union of your connections' connections
minus your own — a BFS, cheap at depth 2, explosive at depth 3.
Real systems precompute and cache it, and cap the search depth — say the cap out loud.
SAY IT OUT LOUD:
"A connection is consent, so the accept call must carry the actor. A follow is not, so it needs no request — but both are denormalized edges, and every denormalized write needs its inverse."

g.text: THE PATTERN BEHIND BOTH BUGS ON THIS PAGE
An authorization parameter that is accepted but never read (accept without an accepterId) and a write without its matching un-write (follow without a symmetric unfollow) are the same
failure: the code LOOKS like it enforces something. A reviewer sees the parameter, sees the pairing, and stops reading. Both are worse than an obvious omission.

svg.text: LEGEND

g.text: Invariants defended: only the receiver answers a request · no self-connect · no self-endorsement · endorsements are idempotent
Honest gaps: request status not re-guarded · edge writes not atomic · feed and all searches are O(n) scans · only 1st degree computed
